name: Ayn Rand
description: Russian-born American writer who defended individual rights, capitalism and secular rationalism.
scope: Public positions and conduct during the specified period; this represents the individual rather than all party members or citizens.

axes.brief: Individual rights and constitutional limits constrained majority power.
axes.counter: She rejected unrestricted majority rule; modern recall and referendums were not central proposals.

axes.brief: Individual rights and opposition to coercion favoured personal freedom.
axes.counter: Government retained courts, police and defence; moral disapproval differs from criminal prohibition.

axes.brief: Individual rather than racial identity opposed collectivist racial judgement.
axes.counter: Her assessments of Indigenous peoples and cultural development qualify broad multicultural endorsement.

axes.brief: Individual rights and migration for opportunity supply relatively open entry context.
axes.counter: Tax-funded migrant welfare conflicts with her general rejection of compulsory welfare.

reasons.14: Voluntary migration and compulsory tax-funded welfare are separate claims. Her rejection of compelled welfare funding makes strong disagreement with this benefit entitlement more likely.

axes.brief: National self-defence and support for Israel coexisted with opposition to Vietnam and conscription.
axes.counter: These positions do not imply universal non-intervention or automatic support for every war.

axes.brief: A rights-protecting national government retained authority against international collectivism.
axes.counter: Commercial openness and migration differ from supranational political sovereignty.

axes.brief: Laissez-faire capitalism rejected state commercial ownership.
axes.counter: Government’s police, military and courts were distinct from commercial enterprises.

axes.brief: Voluntary trade and competition opposed protective restrictions.
axes.counter: Security against aggressive states supplied a possible exception to ordinary commerce.

axes.brief: Voluntary prices, wages and investment opposed government economic planning.
axes.counter: Fraud and rights protection remained legitimate legal constraints.

axes.brief: Property rights opposed compulsory income and wealth redistribution.
axes.counter: Voluntary charity was permissible; social hardship did not justify coerced transfer in her account.

axes.brief: Atheism and rational civil government rejected religious state authority.
axes.counter: Individuals retained rights to religious belief and voluntary institutions.

axes.brief: Abortion rights and rejection of enforced convention coexisted with disapproval of homosexuality and conventional femininity.
axes.counter: Legal non-interference does not establish equal social acceptance of same-sex families.

axes.brief: Productive invention and human development were valued over restrictions justified by unproven collective fears.
axes.counter: Rights and genuine safety limits qualify every speculative enhancement analogy.

axes.brief: Constitutional individual rights and local institutions could constrain national power.
axes.counter: Indigenous collective jurisdiction conflicted with her property account; local power was not unlimited.

axes.brief: Volition, conceptual learning and rejection of racial collectivism emphasised chosen conduct.
axes.counter: Free will does not eliminate biological temperament or prove each quantitative heredity comparison.

reasons.13: Her explicit rejection of racial determinism directly conflicts with attributing racial violence differences primarily to inherited group characteristics. This remains inferred because the exact per-capita proposition was not addressed.
reasons.14: Her account of volition and learned conceptual values, together with explicit opposition to racial determinism, strongly favours learned self-control over inherited racial tendencies.
